chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ubayd Allah informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

Abu Abd Allah (عليه السلام) was asked about a man who has contact with a woman in a manner short of the private part: is ghusl obligatory upon her if he ejaculates while she does not ejaculate? He said: There is no ghusl upon her. And if he does not ejaculate, then there is no ghusl upon him.

key_terms.الْفَرْجِ: the private part; here, indicating actual intercourse as distinct from lesser intimate contact
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: ritual bath required in certain states of janabah
key_terms.فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ غُسْلٌ: ghusl is not obligatory upon him in the stated circumstance
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهَا غُسْلٌ: ghusl is not obligatory upon her in this case

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl required if intimacy occurs short of intercourse and only one spouse ejaculates?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning intimacy short of vaginal intercourse and the obligation of ghusl. It states that if the man ejaculates and the woman does not, ghusl is not obligatory upon her, and if he does not ejaculate, then ghusl is not obligatory upon him.
